title: Decision: Reinstatement of the Rights and Privileges of the Syrian Arab Republic
text:
CS-2025-5387(E) distributed 28/11/2025 
*CS-2025-5387.E* 
 
 
OPCW 
Conference of the States Parties 
Thirtieth Session 
24 – 28 November 2025 
C-30/DEC.8 
28 November 2025 
Original: ENGLISH 
DECISION 
REINSTATEMENT OF THE RIGHTS AND PRIVILEGES  
OF THE SYRIAN ARAB REPUBLIC 
The Conference of the States Parties, 
Recalling its decision C-25/DEC.9 (dated 21 April 2021) addressing the possession and use of 
chemical weapons by the Syrian Arab Republic, including the suspension of the Syrian Arab 
Republic’s rights and privileges under the Chemical Weapons Convention (the Convention) 
until the Director-General reports to the Executive Council (the Council) that the Syrian Arab 
Republic has completed all of the measures contained in paragraph 5 of Council decision  
EC-94/DEC.2 (dated 9 July 2020); 
Recalling also that the Council, at its 110th Session, adopted a decision, submitted by Qatar, 
concerning the “Expedited On-Site Destruction of Any Remnants of Chemical Weapons in the 
Syrian Arab Republic” (EC-110/DEC.1, dated 8 October 2025), and encouraged the 
Conference of the States Parties, in view of the recent positive developments, to revisit its 
decision C-25/DEC.9 in the event of continued and sustained progress in the elimination of any 
remaining chemical weapons in the Syrian Arab Republic; and 
Noting the regular notes by the Director-General detailing the constructive and positive 
cooperation demonstrated by the new Government of the Syrian Arab Republic in its 
engagement with the Technical Secretariat; 
Hereby: 
1. 
Decides to delegate to the Council the authority, taking into account any progress made, 
to consider and decide on the reinstatement of the suspended rights and privileges of 
the Syrian Arab Republic under the Convention;  
2. 
Recognises that the purpose of this decision is to respond to the specific circumstances 
in the Syrian Arab Republic and that this decision does not create any precedent for the 
future; and 
3. 
Decides to remain seized of this matter.
